name: The ascent through the inner regions (Sant Mat)

stages.name: nām-dān and the vows
stages.description: Initiation by a living master; vegetarian diet, abstinence, moral life, daily meditation.

stages.name: tīsrā til (eye centre)
stages.description: Simran and dhyān gather the attention at the eye centre; the body is left behind as at death.

stages.name: Sahasdal Kanwal
stages.description: First region; bell and conch; the flame of Jot Nirañjan; the astral region.

stages.name: Trikuṭī
stages.description: Region of Brahm and the universal mind; drum/thunder; the causal region, still within Kāl's domain.

stages.name: Daswān Dwār / Sunn
stages.description: The soul, free of the three bodies and the mind, sees itself as spirit ('self-realization'); sārangī.

stages.name: Mahāsunn
stages.description: A region of darkness crossed only with the master's help.

stages.name: Bhanwar Guphā
stages.description: Flute.

stages.name: Sach Khand / Sat Lok
stages.description: The soul meets the Sat Purush ('God-realization'); vīṇā; beyond the reach of birth and death.

stages.name: Alakh Lok and Agam Lok
stages.description: Higher purely spiritual regions.

stages.name: Anāmī / Radhasoami Dhām
stages.description: The supreme, the ocean from which the soul came.

notes: Beas-line version. Sant Mat itself holds that the absorption of other yogas ends at Sahasdal Kanwal or Trikuṭī (B4 here); it would reject any alignment of those regions with liberation.

name: The three stages of the Sahajiyā path

stages.name: pravarta
stages.description: Reliance on the name (nāma) and the guru's mantra; ordinary Vaiṣṇava practice.

stages.name: sādhaka
stages.description: Reliance on bhāva; the esoteric discipline with the partner begins (restricted; not described).

stages.name: siddha
stages.description: Resting in prema; the sahaja state of the innate Man.

notes: Scheme (pravarta–sādhaka–siddha, with the āśrayas of nāma, bhāva, prema) widely reported for Sahajiyā manuals; some sources add a preliminary 'sthūla' stage (low confidence).

name: The order of the aṅgas in the Rajasthani Sant anthologies

stages.name: gurudev
stages.description: Meeting and honouring the true guru.

stages.name: sumiran
stages.description: Remembrance of the Name.

stages.name: birah
stages.description: The burning of separation.

stages.name: gyān-birah
stages.description: Separation turned to knowledge (Kabīr Granthāvalī).

stages.name: paracā
stages.description: Direct encounter with the Lord: light, unstruck sound, nectar.

stages.name: ras / jarṇā / hairān
stages.description: Tasting the Lord, bearing it quietly, wonder.

stages.name: lai
stages.description: Absorption (laya) in the Lord.

notes: CAUTION: this is the editorial order of topics in the Dādūpanthī anthologies (Kabīr Granthāvalī, Dādū Vāṇī), not a ladder the texts themselves declare; recorded because the order recurs and reads as a progression. Aṅga names moderate-to-low confidence.

stages.name: mānas jap
stages.description: Mental repetition of the name.

stages.name: mānas dhyān
stages.description: Contemplating the guru's or deity's form.

stages.name: dṛṣṭi yoga
stages.description: Fixing the gaze at a point within, opening the inner light.

stages.name: nādānusandhān
stages.description: Following the inner sounds to the soundless.

stages.name: niḥśabda
stages.description: Beyond sound: realization of the Supreme.
